description: Brown stone with a wood grain and two dark knots. Nothing that grows has been caught carrying one.
lore: It is not a rare stone. That is the whole of the difficulty. A collector three months in owns one, because they are cheap and they keep turning up, and any dealer with a bench has two or three under the cloth. It passes every test the trade has: warm within a breath of the hand, no chip under a bench hammer, pale glassy seams that take a setting cleanly. In a plate it does what it promises — the blow arrives smaller, and fire arrives smaller still, which is the joke every buyer makes about a stone with a grain in it, and the joke is most of why they sell.

By [[lore/the_hard_pieces|the rule of the thing]], one kind of creature leaves one kind of stone. Nothing that grows has ever been broken carrying one of these. Not a standing shape out of the black wood, not a root thing out of the fen, nothing anybody has ever put a bag under.

[[characters/a6d7323d|Gunnar]] has walked more of this country than the rest of them together and keeps what he measures to himself. Somebody asked him straight, at the fire, in front of people, whether he had ever in his life seen a thing of wood get up and go anywhere. He said no. He was asked whether that settled it. He said it settled where he had been.
gm_notes: Unbound stone, handled as ordinary rather than eerie: the cheapness is the horror, because there are a great many of them and no account of a single one's origin. Nothing is asserted to exist. Gunnar's answer is exact and useless on purpose — he does not speculate, and the gap stays open for a later reveal or for nothing at all.
